investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-29T00:51:19–53Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents. Because the failure is shared across all sibling checks with the exact same error message, the fault is localized to the swarm gateway or its upstream ELB, not to any individual check's logic or eval runner code.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST /api/agents → swarm gateway /v1/agents call as its first step; when that gateway returns a connection error, no agent is provisioned, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is collected, and all three checks fail with code bad_gateway. The root cause is a connectivity or availability failure at the swarm gateway layer, not in the eval runner or expected-output contract definitions.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=503 exceeds max 300)
investigations.summary: The published observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was last generated 503 minutes ago, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an eval-layer failure localized to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks passed, indicating no broader site outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot on disk is structurally valid (schemaVersion=1, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true, featureCount=19) but is 503 minutes old, causing the snapshotAgeMinutes assertion in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) to fail. The root cause is a missed or failed scheduled workflow execution, not a problem with the snapshot content format or the eval runner logic itself.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 503' — the sole violated assertion, directly reported by the eval runner (evidenceItem: failed-check.message).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=503, maxAgeMinutes=300, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — all other assertions passed; only the age bound was breached (evidenceItem: failed-check.evidence).

expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the exact contract boundary that was crossed (evidenceItem: expected-output.contract).

sibling checks public-observability-page, public-models-page, and public-marketing-pages all passed with HTTP 200 responses, ruling out a shared infrastructure or hosting failure (evidenceItems: sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages).

source=github-actions in the snapshot evidence confirms the snapshot is expected to be produced by a GitHub Actions workflow, making a missed or failed workflow run the most direct explanation for the staleness (evidenceItem: failed-check.evidence).

The check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational in infra/evals/status/features.json line 383, confirming this failure does not constitute a product outage (evidenceItem: source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383).
possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot failed, was skipped, or was not triggered for at least 503 minutes, leaving the previously published snapshot in place.
Second: The GitHub Actions workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a job step error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) before writing a fresh snapshot to the published URL.
Third: A GitHub Actions runner quota, concurrency limit, or repository-level workflow disable caused the scheduled run to be queued but never executed.
Fourth: The GitHub Pages deployment step succeeded but published a cached or previously-built artifact rather than the freshly generated snapshot, resulting in an unchanged timestamp.
